title: Delegates, events, and lambdas — map
intro: This module teaches how C# expresses callbacks. A delegate is a typed method reference; Func and Action cover most cases. Lambdas write handlers inline but may capture variables in a closure. Events restrict who can subscribe and raise. C# 14 extension members add helpers to existing types. Compare with JavaScript functions and EventTarget throughout.

conceptCards.title: Delegates, Func, and Action
conceptCards.summary: A delegate is a type that holds a method reference. Func returns a value; Action returns void. Multicast combines handlers with +=.

conceptCards.title: Lambdas and closures
conceptCards.summary: Lambdas are inline anonymous functions. Capturing outer variables creates a closure. static lambdas forbid capture.

conceptCards.title: Local functions
conceptCards.summary: Named helpers inside a method. Support yield return and recursion. Prefer over lambdas when you call directly without a delegate.

conceptCards.title: Events
conceptCards.summary: Publisher raises; subscribers += and -= only. Safer than a public delegate field. Unsubscribe the same instance to avoid leaks.

conceptCards.title: Extension members
conceptCards.summary: Static helpers with instance syntax. C# 14 adds extension properties. Real instance members always win at bind time.

conceptCards.title: JS first-class functions
conceptCards.summary: JavaScript functions are values natively. C# needs delegate conversion. EventTarget maps to C# events with same-reference unsubscribe.
